newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU officials to discuss U.S. rice dispute Thursday.
newsitem.headline: EU officials to discuss U.S. rice dispute Thursday.

text.p: European Union cereals officials will on Thursday debate the latest developments in their rice dispute with the United States, an EU official said on Wednesday.
"The European Commission clearly intend to try to move the issues forward in this weeks's management committee but they appear to be somewhat optimistic," the official said.
The United States has been angered about two issues arising from GATT agreements on rice imports into the EU.
One problem is a Commission proposal for what is called culmulative recovery of tariff payments.
This would offset duties overcharged in a one-year trading period against credits for duties on shipments below the reference price.
"This sounds like a good idea but it would be a nightmare to administrate," the official added.
The U.S. has also been angered by the EU's failure to introduce implementing legislation for tariff-free quotas for 38,000 tonnes of milled rice and 8,000 tonnes of brown rice.
This has prevented the opening of the GATT reduced tariff quota agreement designed to compensate U.S. exporters for trade losses after the EU's enlargement in 1995.
This week's management committee meeting is not expected to reach any agreement on this aspect of the transatlantic trade row.
"There is not much chance of anything going through on this point because the Commission has not produced a proposal in time for member states experts to study it," the official explained.
